invariant_argument: Both PartialDynamics inputs are already admitted, nonempty, and checked for shape and range. Their first transition row exists even when there are zero inputs. Joint pairs must be nonempty, unique, and inside both real carriers; internal unavailable sinks are excluded. Work admission runs first, then relation admission, then validation of every operation, then joint closure in row-major order. A later invalid operation therefore takes priority over an earlier missing pair. The extracted phases preserve the original result and error order.

The declared accounting expression is B=(p+1)^2 and cost=B*(operation_count+1)+(left_states+1)^2*(left_inputs+1)+(right_states+1)^2*(right_inputs+1). Every addition and product is checked. Overflow or cost greater than max_cells returns WorkLimit before relation construction; equality succeeds. This is an admission accounting rule, rather than a bound on all heap bytes, runtime, or executed operations. Direct private-helper tests cover arithmetic overflow without allocating huge models.

The pair map assigns each unique admitted pair its supplied row index. Left and Right operations change exactly one coordinate. A local None remains genuinely unavailable. A defined target must occur in the relation; a missing target returns NotClosed with its original row, operation, and target pair. Interaction entries are supplied premises with exactly one valid Option index per row. Borrowed context and Result collection preserve the original row and operation order. On failure only temporary output is dropped. Lean proves the abstract lookup and closure distinction; Rust indexing and error fields remain separate source obligations.

Local profiles use the actual reviewed component behavioral quotients, including their distinct unavailable sinks. Pair coordinates select only real component states. A profile is the pair of component class IDs, rather than their raw report IDs. First-occurrence interning gives equal joint readouts exactly when profiles agree. Actual PartialDynamics admission checks the complete derived table. Interactions can introduce distinctions within a local profile fiber; they are supplied data, with no inferred independence or commutativity law.

The actual joint quotient refines the initial profile kernel and preserves every finite-word answer and availability distinction by the reviewed provider argument. Equal profiles with different final classes therefore identify exactly a lost joint-future distinction. Analysis scans right row r in increasing order and left row l<r in increasing order. The provider then returns the shortest lexicographic separating word and exact saved answers. The totalized joint system has p+1 states and at most (p+1)^2 ordered state pairs, so B admits the whole search frontier when allocation succeeds. No collision means joint-future observations factor through the realized profiles. The new Lean fiber lemmas and the existing provider proofs support different parts of this argument.

JointDynamics owns immutable admitted pairs, profiles, dynamics, and the checked pair budget, with borrowed getters and no Deserialize or Default bypass. Analysis is a raw mutable report. Verification recomputes the complete analysis and compares refinement and collision. It checks the result on self, without authenticating an external declaration or request hash. Distinct relations can have identical analyses: the native constant, zero-input example uses [(0,0)] and [(1,0)] and accepts cross-verification. The documentation now states this ceiling.

Private helper calls use already admitted ranges and concrete usize values. Budget, relation, operation, transition, and profile phases retain their original order. Output rows, profiles, dense readouts, and owned provider quotients are required results. One pair map and one profile interning map are built outside cell processing. Result collection may allocate output capacity differently from push loops; no allocation-count, heap-totality, or arbitrary-callback guarantee is made. The max_cells expression does not replace the providers own stated cost and trust boundaries.
